title: File Locksmith crashes in some cases when scanning an executable
author: avi12

status.label: File Locksmith crash fixes already active
status.detail: The executable-scan crash belongs to the actively tracked File Locksmith crash family, which has one merged targeted fix and two open isolation/hang-recovery fixes.

next_action.label: Track the existing File Locksmith fixes
next_action.reason: Do not create a competing design while the linked crash work is active.

judgment.rationale: The public timeline links this report to the broader File Locksmith crash tracker and focused crash reports. Concrete upstream fixes already cover disappearing process images and handle-enumeration/interop isolation.
evidence: Issue 45158 is the open File Locksmith crash tracker.
PR 48719 merged a guard for crashes when a listed process image disappears.
PRs 49502 and 50217 remain open for interop access-violation and handle-enumeration isolation.
A commenter reports the symptom disappeared after updating the .NET 10 SDK, which is useful environment evidence but not a separate PowerToys fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Follow the existing File Locksmith crash PRs and revalidate this report against their merged behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: Multiple concrete upstream implementations already cover the crash mechanisms represented by the linked File Locksmith reports.

issue_context.summary: The executable-scan crash belongs to the actively tracked File Locksmith crash family, which has one merged targeted fix and two open isolation/hang-recovery fixes.
known_information: The issue supplies a recording and last-run log for a crash while scanning an executable.
Resource Monitor also struggled to inspect the same file, suggesting a difficult process/file inspection case.
The linked crash family has merged and open implementation PRs.
inferences: This report may be covered by one of the existing disappearing-image, interop, or handle-enumeration fixes, but the public issue does not identify which crash signature occurred.
issue_context.analysis: Existing upstream crash work is stronger ownership evidence than a new speculative plan. Revalidation should compare the original crash signature with the linked fixes after they merge.
initial_investigation: Read the body, last-run-log link, comment, timeline cross-references, and current artifact.
Checked the states of issues 45158, 48693, and 49501 and PRs 48719, 49502, and 50217.
